To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we designed, fabricated, and tested optomechanics that implement an optical backplane for a hybrid self-electro-optic device-based free-space optical interconnect.
we have designed and fabricated optomechanics that are scalable to a full 6U V-Me backplane, that are easy to assemble, and that have a very low optical insertion loss.
the optomechanical system is scalable to a large number of optical channels and that the optical performance of the optoelectronic modules is not affected by the optomechanic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and development of optomechanical components for a four-stage free-space optical backplaned VME chassis.
the design and fabrication of a free-space optical interconnect for a hybrid-self-electrooptic-device-based optical backplane.
the design, fabrication and testing of optoelectronics packaging and optomechanical components for free-space optical backplanes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the optomechanical design and fabrication process presented in this dissertation can be used as a basis for future optomechanics design and fabrication.
the optomechanical design presented in this work is a significant step toward realizing a scalable, high-performance, free-space optical interconnect.
the optomechanical design and fabrication techniques presented here can be used to build a scalable, low-cost, high-performance, and high-reliability optical interconnect.

the design and fabrication of optomechanical components for hybrid-self-electro- optic-device-based free-space-optical interconnects is a challenging and interesting task.
optomechanics are a critical component of any free-space optical backplanes and that the design, fabrication and testing of opto-mechanics is a challenging and important area for future research.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the design of optomechanical structures for optical backplanes is a multidisciplinary problem that requires a thorough understanding of the mechanical, optical, thermal, material and manufacturing aspects of optomechanisms.

optomechanics can be designed and fabricated for hybrid-self-electrooptical-device-based (HSEOD-based) free-space optical interconnects, and that they can be used to implement optical interconnects with high optical and mechanical performance.
